probes.code: async function loadJson(fetcher, url) { try { const response = await fetcher(url); if (!response.ok) return { ok: false, kind: 'http', status: response.status }; try { return { ok: true, data: await response.json() }; } catch { return { ok: false, kind: 'json' }; } } catch { return { ok: false, kind: 'network' }; } } const fixtures = { success: async () => new Response('{"name":"Ada"}', { status: 200, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } }), missing: async () => new Response('{"error":"missing"}', { status: 404, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } }), invalid: async () => new Response('{bad json', { status: 200, headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' } }), network: async () => { throw new TypeError('network'); } }; const result = {}; for (const [name, fixture] of Object.entries(fixtures)) result[name] = await loadJson(fixture, '/users'); console.log(JSON.stringify(result));
probes.description: Controlled Response fixtures for 200 JSON, 404, invalid JSON and rejected network request

questions.question: Jak połączyć semantykę metody GET, status HTTP i reprezentację JSON?
Jak rozdzielić błąd sieci, nieudany status HTTP i błąd parsowania JSON?

excerpts.text: A Response reports whether its status is an ok status; a network failure is represented as a network error.
The Body json method parses the body bytes as JSON and can reject when parsing fails.
GET requests transfer a current representation of the target resource.
The request method token indicates the purpose of the request and the expected meaning of a successful result.
A JSON value is an object, array, number, string, true, false or null.
Object member names should be unique for interoperable behavior.
